items.stem: Based on the chapter, draft a ‘societal sketch’ of the indigenous fan makers. What traits, challenges, and triumphs define their community in the modern era?
items.answer: Based on the text, the indigenous fan makers emerge as a highly resilient, hardworking, and exceptionally creative community. Historically, they were essential contributors to society, providing basic cooling utilities for both grand royal courts and everyday households. Faced with the severe threat of modern cooling technology, these artisans demonstrated remarkable adaptability. Rather than abandoning their ancestral skills, they ingeniously balanced ancient techniques with innovative designs, transforming their craft into a thriving commercial business. They take immense pride in their work, utilizing local materials to reflect their distinct regional identities. Furthermore, through pankha-making workshops, they actively exhibit a forward-looking mindset, deeply committed to passing their precious heritage down to younger generations to ensure its survival.

items.stem: How does the transition of the pankha from a “daily utility item” to a “cultural good” highlight the changing priorities and aesthetics of the modern Indian consumer?
items.answer: The transition of the pankha from a “daily utility item” to a “cultural good” profoundly highlights the evolving priorities of the modern Indian consumer. In the past, the primary consumer need was purely functional: surviving the harsh climatic heat. Today, that basic need is efficiently met by advanced electric appliances. Consequently, the modern consumer’s priority has shifted towards aesthetic appreciation, heritage preservation, and interior decoration. Buyers now seek products that offer a deep connection to their traditional roots and cultural identity. By purchasing these exotic, intricately designed fans as art pieces, modern consumers actively demonstrate a desire to support sustainable indigenous livelihoods and creatively celebrate the rich, diverse artistic history of their nation. items.stem: Discuss the central theme of the chapter “Winds of Change.” How does the journey of the ‘pankha’ mirror the resilience of traditional Indian handicrafts in the face of modernization?
items.answer: The central theme of “Winds of Change” is the evolution, preservation, and enduring cultural significance of the traditional Indian hand fan. The journey of the ‘pankha’ perfectly mirrors the resilience of Indian handicrafts. Initially born out of pure climatic necessity, the craft faced a severe existential threat from modern technology like electric fans and air conditioners. However, instead of fading into obscurity, the craft adapted. Artisans innovated by elevating the pankha from a mere cooling tool to a beautiful decorative artefact. This transition highlights a broader narrative: traditional Indian crafts can survive modernization not by competing on utility, but by intelligently rebranding themselves as symbols of heritage, thereby providing a sustainable livelihood for hardworking indigenous artisans.

items.stem: Imagine you are an elderly artisan from Rajasthan who has been making zardozi and brass fans for decades. Write a diary entry expressing your feelings about how the demand for your craft has changed over the years.
items.answer: Dear Diary, Today, as I wove golden zardozi threads into a new fan, I reflected on the rapid passage of time. Decades ago, our engraved brass fans were essential items used by everyone to beat the scorching Rajasthani heat. When electric coolers arrived, my heart sank. I thought our ancestral craft would vanish forever. But the ‘winds of change’ surprised us all! People now seek my creations not for cooling, but to elegantly adorn their modern homes. They deeply value our royal heritage and intricate designs. Though the fan’s primary purpose has shifted, I am filled with immense pride knowing that my art survives, providing a sustainable livelihood for my family, and keeping our glorious traditions alive. Bhawani

items.stem: You are a cultural heritage advocate. Write a short speech to be delivered at a school assembly, urging students to support local artisans and value traditional crafts like the pankha over mass- produced goods.
items.answer: Respected Principal, Teachers, and friends, Today, I wish to speak about our responsibility towards India’s artistic heritage. Consider the traditional ‘pankha’. Once an everyday necessity, it was nearly eradicated by modern electric appliances. Yet, it survived because hardworking artisans brilliantly transformed it into a decorative artefact. The continued survival of such crafts depends entirely on us. When we purchase a handmade palm-leaf fan from Kerala or a bamboo fan from Bihar, we are not merely buying decor; we are providing a sustainable livelihood for rural communities. We are instilling immense pride in indigenous creators. Let us pledge to actively support local artisans, appreciate the history behind their crafts, and keep our cultural roots vibrantly alive. Thank you.

This marks the beginning of a hilarious and exhausting secret mission for Ravi, who attempts to play the role of a detective trailing a suspect. A Day of Rule-Breaking and Adventures Unaware—or so it seems—that he is being followed, Grandpa goes on a fun, independent stroll across the city. He first visits a children’s park, where he buys a paper-cone of peanuts and happily watches the children play. Next, he stops at a tea stall and treats himself to items that are strictly banned by Ravi’s mother: a sugary cup of tea, two bananas, and an ice cream! While Grandpa is having a great time, poor Ravi struggles to stay hidden. He faces continuous humiliation and physical discomfort. He has to duck behind cars, crouch behind elephant-shaped bushes, crawl on all fours, face the anger of street vendors, and even gets kicked out of a ladies’ hair salon while trying to keep his grandfather in sight. The Great Escape Eventually, Grandpa walks briskly to a bus stop and boards a bus. Ravi rushes in after him, keeping his eyes glued to Grandpa’s signature yellow cap. However, to Ravi’s absolute horror, he discovers that the person wearing the yellow cap is a complete stranger! Grandpa had cleverly swapped his cap with someone else to trick his grandson and successfully managed to ditch him. A Heartwarming Relief and a Clever Twist Sick with worry that Grandpa is lost in the big city, Ravi returns home in a panic. However, to his immense delight and relief, he finds Grandpa safely asleep in his bed, snoring peacefully. Overwhelmed with love and realizing how much he truly cares for his grandfather, Ravi kneels by the bed and gives him a heartfelt hug. When Ravi’s mother questions them, Grandpa coolly covers for Ravi, saying he had a quiet morning but that Ravi had mysteriously disappeared. Then, Grandpa brings out a gift- wrapped parcel for Ravi. Ravi’s mother is impatient, thinking Grandpa’s memory is failing since Ravi’s birthday was three months ago. However, it is actually Grandpa’s own birthday, and he is keeping up his lifelong tradition of giving gifts to his family on his special day. The Irony of “Vitamin-M” When Ravi opens the gift, he finds a detective storybook. Grandpa gives him a mischievous wink and playfully advises him to read the tips on how to trail a suspect without being fooled. This proves that Grandpa’s memory and wit are perfectly sharp; he knew Ravi was following him all along and decided to teach him a playful lesson. The story ends on a humorous and ironic note regarding the title, “Vitamin-M” (which stands for a memory vitamin). While Ravi’s mother constantly worries about Grandpa’s fading memory, she is the one who completely forgot her own father’s birthday, proving that she might be the one who actually needs “Vitamin-M”!

items.answer: Age-based discrimination can be seen in everyday situations. For example, in a classroom discussion, a younger student may share an idea or opinion, but the teacher or classmates may ignore it, thinking the student is too young to understand the topic properly. Later, when an older student gives a similar idea, it is taken more seriously. In this case, the younger student’s opinion is disregarded not because it is wrong, but simply because of their age. This shows how people can be judged unfairly based on how young or old they are, rather than on the value of their ideas. Our elderly inspire us through their unparalleled resilience and vast reservoirs of experience. For instance, my own grandfather, despite his failing physical health, never fails to recall the most intricate details of his youth, teaching us the value of observing the world closely. As the famous writer Gabriel García Márquez implied, the wisdom of old age is the light that guides the youth. Whether it is a forgotten traditional recipe that holds a family together, or tales of navigating a world without modern technology, they teach us patience, gratitude, and the importance of human connection over materialistic pursuits. They have faced challenges that our generation can barely fathom—from surviving historical economic hardships to adapting to radical technological shifts. Watching them overcome these immense life changes with grace and a smile has an incredibly inspiring impact on me. It makes our modern-day academic and social challenges seem much more manageable. Their ability to find joy in the simple things, like a quiet morning walk or a family dinner, teaches us how to remain grounded. In conclusion, our elderly are not a burden to be managed, but a treasure to be cherished. As we rush towards the future, it is vital to pause and hold the hands of those who built the very foundation we stand upon. items.stem: Read the extract given below and answer the questions that follows : “It was only last month that Ravi’s Grandpa had come to live with them because he was getting too old to live on his own. It had been a difficult month with Grandpa having to be admitted to the hospital because he absent-mindedly took a double dose of his medicines, and then gave them several anxious moments when he got lost on one occasion he went for a walk and forgot the way back home.” i. What underlying reason prompted Grandpa’s move to his daughter’s house? (a) Inability to live independently (b) Sudden financial instability (c) Desire to meet his grandson (d) Lack of medical facilities ii. Statement I: Grandpa intentionally took extra medicines to get attention. Statement II: The family experienced a highly stressful first month with him. (a) Both I and II are true. (b) Both I and II are false. (c) I is true, II is false. (d) I is false, II is true. iii. What two incidents made the family’s first month with Grandpa difficult? iv. Identify the word from the extract that means “without paying attention” or “forgetfully”. v. State whether True or False with a 1-sentence reason: Grandpa was highly familiar with the neighborhood around his daughter’s house.
items.answer: i. (a) Inability to live independently ii. (d) I is false, II is true. iii. Grandpa accidentally took a double dose of medicines and got lost while going for a walk. iv. absent-mindedly v. False, because he got lost on one occasion while taking a walk and forgot his way back home.

items.section_heading: You must have read stories about taking care of
items.stem: Based on the story, provide a detailed character sketch of Grandpa. How does he balance his vulnerability with his sharp wit? NODIA
items.answer: Grandpa is a resilient, witty, and deeply independent elderly man who struggles with the loss of his autonomy. Having moved to a bustling city after a fall, he initially appears vulnerable, plagued by a slightly failing memory. However, he fiercely refuses to be treated like a prisoner by his patronising daughter. Beneath his frail exterior lies a remarkably sharp, mischievous mind. He cleverly outsmarts his grandson, Ravi, by swapping his signature yellow cap with a stranger on a bus, proving he is far from helpless. Furthermore, he is incredibly generous and warm- hearted, maintaining the beautiful tradition of giving gifts to others on his own birthday. Ultimately, Grandpa asserts his dignity through humor, intelligence, and a quiet rebellion against overprotective rules.

items.section_heading: You must have read stories about taking care of
items.stem: Analyze the character of Ravi’s mother. Do her intentions justify her treatment of Grandpa?
items.answer: Ravi’s mother represents the classic dilemma of adult children caring for aging parents. Her intentions are undoubtedly rooted in genuine love and concern; she naturally worries about his safety after he slips in the garden and forgets his route home. However, her execution is deeply flawed. She uses a loud, patronising tone and imposes strict dietary and mobility rules, effectively stripping him of his dignity and making him feel like a prisoner. Her obsession with his “fading memory” and “Vitamin-M” blinds her to his emotional needs for independence and respect. The ultimate irony of her character is exposed when she completely forgets her own father’s birthday, highlighting that her clinical, rule-based care severely lacks emotional attentiveness.

items.section_heading: You must have read stories about taking care of
items.stem: The story beautifully highlights the clash between elderly independence and overprotective caregiving. Discuss how this theme is developed throughout the narrative.
items.answer: The narrative masterfully explores the delicate balance between keeping an elderly parent safe and respecting their autonomy. When Grandpa moves to the city, his daughter’s overprotective rules stifle him. She bans his favorite snacks and covertly sends Ravi to track him, treating him like an incapable child. However, Grandpa’s rebellious morning stroll—where he joyfully buys roasted peanuts, sugary tea, and ice cream— symbolizes his desperate craving for simple freedoms. By outsmarting Ravi at the bus stop, Grandpa reclaims his agency, proving that older adults still possess sharp wits and a desire for self-determination. The story suggests that while physical care is essential, emotional respect and the freedom to enjoy life’s small pleasures are equally crucial for the elderly.

items.section_heading: You must have read stories about taking care of
items.stem: Imagine you are Ravi. Write a diary entry expressing your feelings of guilt about how your mother treats Grandpa and your subsequent failure as a “secret detective.”
items.answer: Dear Diary, Today has been a total rollercoaster of emotions. I feel a deep knot of guilt in my stomach every time Mom speaks to Grandpa in that loud, patronising tone. He is a grown man, yet she treats him like a prisoner in our own home! When she assigned me the “secret mission” to tail him, I felt terrible, but I went along with it anyway. I crawled behind elephant-shaped bushes and even got kicked out of a hair salon, genuinely thinking I was a master detective. Imagine my absolute horror when the man in the yellow cap turned out to be a complete stranger! Grandpa totally outsmarted me. Seeing him snoring peacefully at home later was the biggest relief of my life. Ravi

items.section_heading: You must have read stories about taking care of
items.stem: Describe the climax of the story at the bus stop. How does this event shift the power dynamic between Grandpa and Ravi?
items.answer: The climax occurs when Grandpa briskly walks to a bus stop, fully aware that Ravi is clumsily tailing him through the city. As Ravi keeps his eyes glued to Grandpa’s signature yellow cap, Grandpa masterfully executes a classic bait- and-switch by swapping his cap with a complete stranger boarding the bus. This brilliant moment decisively shifts the power dynamic. Until now, Ravi and his mother held the illusion of control, believing Grandpa was a helpless old man needing surveillance. By orchestrating this clever escape, Grandpa reclaims his authority and proves his cognitive sharpness. It deeply humbles Ravi, who transitions from a confident “secret detective” to a panic-stricken boy, restoring Grandpa’s position as the wise patriarch. Downloaded from www.pdf.tube
